title: Evaluation on weakly contractible affines is conservative
statement:
Let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and let $\mathcal W$ be the
class of affine weakly contractible objects of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$.

1. A sequence $A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C$ of $\mathcal R$-modules with $g\circ f=0$
   is exact at $B$ if and only if $A(W)\to B(W)\to C(W)$ is exact for every
   $W\in\mathcal W$.
2. A complex of $\mathcal R$-modules is acyclic if and only if its evaluation at every
   $W\in\mathcal W$ is acyclic.
3. A morphism of $\mathcal R$-modules is an isomorphism if and only if its evaluation at
   every $W\in\mathcal W$ is bijective; a morphism of complexes is a quasi-isomorphism if and
   only if its evaluation at every $W\in\mathcal W$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: First record precisely the local lifting criterion for module exactness. Put $Z=\ker(g)$ and let $u:A\to Z$ be induced by $f$; its existence follows from $gf=0$. The sequence is exact at $B$ precisely when $\operatorname{coker}(u)=Z/\operatorname{im}(f)=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1), the underlying abelian sheaf of this cokernel is the abelian cokernel of $u$. Faithfulness reflects the zero object: if the identity of its underlying object is zero then the identity of the module is zero. Hence exactness is equivalent to the underlying abelian map $u$ being epic. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] this is equivalent to local lifting of every section of $Z$. Finally $Z(V)=\ker(g(V))$ by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus exactness at $B$ is equivalent to: every $b\in B(V)$ with $g(b)=0$ lifts through $f$ on some covering of $V$. This argument applies to any sheaf of rings, without commutativity.

By [det-pe-wcb-cover], every site object $V$ admits a covering $\{W_i\to V\}$ with $W_i=\operatorname{Spec}D_i$ and $D_i$ w-contractible. The last assertion of [det-pe-weak-contractible-equivalences] says each such affine is weakly contractible. Consequently every $V$ has a covering by objects of $\mathcal W$. Only this inclusion is used; we do not assume the converse between ring-theoretic w-contractibility and weak contractibility of an affine site object.

source.place: Tag 0947 (proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles), covering hypothesis; blueprint proof, first paragraph

proof.text: Assume the sequence is exact and fix any $W\in\mathcal W$. In step 1 the underlying abelian map $u:A\to Z$ is locally surjective. Its underlying map of sheaves of sets is therefore epic by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective]. Part 3 of [det-pe-weak-contractible-equivalences] makes $A(W)\to Z(W)$ surjective. Since $Z(W)=\ker(g(W))$ by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], every element of the evaluated kernel is in the image of $f(W)$; the opposite inclusion follows from $gf=0$. This proves the forward implication of clause 1 for every affine weakly contractible $W$, not only those furnished by the ring-theoretic covering theorem.

source.place: Tags 0946 (lemma-w-contractible), part (1), and 0947, proof of (1); set epi criterion Tag 00WN

proof.text: Conversely, suppose the evaluated sequence is exact for every $W\in\mathcal W$. Given $b\in B(V)$ with $g(b)=0$, take the covering $\{W_i\to V\}$ of step 2. Exactness on $W_i$ gives $a_i\in A(W_i)$ with $f(a_i)=b|_{W_i}$. The sections $a_i$ need not agree on overlaps: step 1 requires only local lifts. It therefore proves exactness at $B$, completing clause 1.

For any cochain complex $K$, its cohomology object in degree $q$ is $\ker(d^q)/\operatorname{im}(d^{q-1})$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It vanishes exactly when $K^{q-1}\to K^q\to K^{q+1}$ is exact. Apply clause 1 for each $q\in\mathbf Z$; exchanging the two universal quantifiers $q$ and $W$ proves clause 2. No boundedness hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 0115 (definition-quasi-isomorphism-cochain), part (2), and the preceding formula for cohomology

proof.text: An isomorphism of module sheaves has bijective components, by evaluating its inverse. Conversely suppose $\varphi(W)$ is bijective for every $W\in\mathcal W$. Cover an arbitrary $V$ as in step 2. If $\varphi(s)=\varphi(t)$ in $N(V)$, injectivity on each covering member makes $s|_{W_i}=t|_{W_i}$, whence $s=t$ by the sheaf condition. Thus $\varphi$ is injective on sections of every object. Given $n\in N(V)$, choose the unique lifts $m_i\in M(W_i)$. Their restrictions agree on $W_i\times_VW_j$ by the injectivity just proved for all objects. The sheaf condition glues them to $m\in M(V)$ with $\varphi(m)=n$. Hence every component is bijective. Its inverse is linear and commutes with restrictions, since applying $\varphi$ verifies both assertions and $\varphi$ is injective. These inverses define the inverse morphism of module sheaves, proving the first assertion of clause 3.

source.place: Proof, clause 3, expanded with the sheaf gluing argument

proof.text: Let $v:K\to L$ be a morphism of complexes and use its cone $C(v)^q=L^q\oplus K^{q+1}$ with differential $(l,k)\mapsto(d_Ll+v(k),-d_Kk)$. By [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic], $v$ is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when $C(v)$ is acyclic; the same lemma applies in the abelian category of $\mathcal R(W)$-modules. Finite biproducts are finite products, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] computes these sectionwise. Evaluation is additive by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so the displayed differential evaluates to precisely the differential of $C(v(W))$. Thus $C(v)(W)\cong C(v(W))$ as complexes. Clause 2 now gives that $v$ is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if every $v(W)$ is, completing clause 3.
